allObjections.title: Operator override creates governance bypass
allObjections.detail: The `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob in CA-13-A v2 allows operators to set GTM bar as low as 75, undermining the CEO directive for ≥95. This creates a permanent escape hatch where operators can ship at 75 indefinitely by never setting the override, making the '≥95 after first product' promise unenforceable.

allObjections.title: Capability-keyed naming loses agent traceability
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B v2's switch to `crawl-write-executor` and `orchestra-admission-executor` obscures which primary agent owns the sibling. When debugging production issues, operators won't know that `crawl-write-executor` belongs to Agent #21 without cross-referencing the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY, increasing operational complexity.

allObjections.title: Phase B prerequisite enforcement unclear
allObjections.detail: §11 Step 5 references 'Phase B pass per CA-14-A canonical' but CA-13-A v2 eliminates the Near-GTM conditional band without clarifying how partial Phase B passes (some paths skipped) affect clearance. The interaction between hard thresholds and Phase B skip-disclosure creates ambiguity about what constitutes a 'pass'.

allObjections.title: No migration path for in-flight products
allObjections.detail: Products currently in the pipeline targeting 75-89 Demo-ready have no documented migration path if their operator later sets `gtm_ready_bar_override: 95`. The proposal doesn't specify whether the override applies retroactively to already-cleared products or only to new clearances, creating versioning confusion.

allObjections.title: Operator-config knob risks inconsistency
allObjections.detail: The introduction of the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob in §7.6 could lead to inconsistencies across products if operators set different thresholds. This could undermine the uniformity of the GTM readiness criteria and complicate governance.

allObjections.title: Elimination of Near-GTM band lacks flexibility
allObjections.detail: By eliminating the 90–94 Near-GTM conditional band, the proposal removes flexibility for products that are close to being market-ready but not quite there. This could delay the launch of products that are otherwise viable with minor adjustments.

allObjections.title: Sibling naming convention may cause confusion
allObjections.detail: Switching to capability-keyed sibling charter naming could cause confusion if the capabilities are not clearly defined or if they overlap with other agents. This might lead to misunderstandings about the roles and responsibilities of each agent.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback strategy in case the implementation of the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob causes unintended consequences. This could lead to difficulties in reverting changes and potentially causing harm to the system.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Testing
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not outline a comprehensive testing plan to ensure the correctness and safety of the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob. This could lead to errors or security vulnerabilities being introduced into the system.

allObjections.title: Inconsistent Authorization
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces a new authorization mechanism for the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob, but it is unclear how this mechanism will interact with existing authorization systems. This could lead to inconsistencies or security vulnerabilities in the authorization process.

allObjections.title: Operator override complexity
allObjections.detail: The introduction of `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` adds complexity to the system. Operators may set arbitrary values without understanding the full implications, leading to inconsistent product quality. The §7.6 score bands should remain canonical and uniform across products to ensure consistency.

allObjections.title: Lack of migration path
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear migration path for existing products that are already in the pipeline. This could lead to inconsistencies and potential failures in the clearance process for products that were initiated under the previous guidelines.

allObjections.title: Potential for misuse
allObjections.detail: The operator-configurable knob could be misused by operators to bypass the strict quality standards set by the canonical §7.6 score bands. This could lead to products being cleared for GTM that do not meet the necessary quality standards, undermining the overall integrity of the system.

allObjections.title: Operator Override Risk
allObjections.detail: The introduction of the `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob allows operators to set a higher GTM readiness bar, but this could lead to inconsistent application of the GTM readiness criteria across different products, potentially undermining the integrity of the GTM process.

allObjections.title: Complexity in Governance
allObjections.detail: The proposal adds another layer of complexity to the governance model by introducing an operator-configurable GTM bar, which may lead to confusion and difficulties in maintaining consistent governance practices across the organization.

allObjections.title: Potential for Abuse
allObjections.detail: The capability-keyed naming for sibling charters could be exploited by operators to bypass certain governance checks, especially if the naming conventions are not strictly enforced or monitored.

allObjections.title: Operator Config Knob Risk
allObjections.detail: The `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob in §7.6 introduces a risk of inconsistent GTM readiness standards across products, potentially leading to customer confusion and diluted brand perception if some products are launched with lower quality scores than others. This undermines the purpose of having a standardized GTM readiness process.

allObjections.title: Clamping Semantics
allObjections.detail: The silent clamping of out-of-bounds `gtm_ready_bar_override` values to [75, 100] in §7.6, while notifying admins, could lead to unexpected behavior and debugging challenges. Operators might assume their configured value is being used, leading to incorrect assumptions about GTM readiness.

allObjections.title: Reconciliation Paragraph Redundancy
allObjections.detail: The §19.0 reconciliation paragraph distinguishing Self-Audit 95/95 from GTM Readiness bar seems redundant, as the §10 governance-mechanisms table already covers these distinctions. This adds unnecessary complexity to the document.

allObjections.title: Sibling Naming Convention
allObjections.detail: While capability-keyed naming for sibling charters is generally better, the specific name `orchestra-admission-executor` might be too specific. It focuses on the 'admission' aspect, potentially overlooking other responsibilities the executor might have in the future.

allObjections.title: §7.6 override risk
allObjections.detail: The operator-configurable GTM bar (gtm_ready_bar_override) lacks enforcement for CEO directives. §7.6 allows operators to set thresholds below the CEO-mandated 95 without consequences, creating misalignment between executive intent and implementation. The clamping mechanism only handles numerical bounds, not policy compliance.

allObjections.title: Sibling naming ambiguity
allObjections.detail: Capability-keyed naming for executors (crawl-write-executor/orchestra-admission-executor) in §15.1 creates ambiguity. Unlike agent-specific names, these don't indicate primary association, risking confusion during incident debugging. The proposal lacks cross-referencing standards between primary agents and siblings.

allObjections.title: HARD threshold fallout
allObjections.detail: Eliminating Near-GTM conditional band ignores operational realities. Products scoring 89 (Demo-ready) but blocked from conditional clearance due to a single high finding may undergo unnecessary rebuilds. §11 Step 5 HARD fails to account for context-dependent risk tolerance.

allObjections.title: Phase B verification gap
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A-CT-4 conformance test only checks for conditional-clearance keywords but doesn't validate Phase B testing requirements. Agent #21's adversarial testing mandate (ENTRY 015) could be bypassed if implementation focuses solely on score thresholds without verifying interactive flow coverage.

allObjections.title: Override weakens global defaults
allObjections.detail: In CA-13-A v2 §7.6, `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` can raise the GTM bar per product while leaving the canonical threshold at 75. That creates a split-brain policy where the same clearance step means different things across products, environments, and operator views, increasing the chance of misconfigured launches and ambiguous audit outcomes.

allObjections.title: Silent clamp hides operator errors
allObjections.detail: The proposed `[75, 100]` clamping in CA-13-A v2 silently converts out-of-bounds values instead of rejecting them. In a governance path, silent coercion is dangerous because a mistaken `50` becomes a seemingly valid `75`, which can mask operational mistakes and make post-incident forensics harder than a hard failure would.

allObjections.title: Hard gate removes recovery path
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A v2 eliminates the 90–94 Near-GTM conditional path from §11 Step 5 entirely. That means a product that is otherwise launchable but temporarily blocked by a narrow, fixable issue cannot use a supervised conditional path, which may increase time-to-market and encourage risky workarounds outside the formal clearance flow.

allObjections.title: Sibling naming still underspecified
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B v2 switches to capability-keyed names like `crawl-write-executor` and `orchestra-admission-executor`, but the draft excerpt truncates the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY definitions and does not fully specify collision handling, lifecycle, or migration from the old keys. Without explicit compatibility rules, this risks orphaned permissions or duplicate executor entries during rollout.

allObjections.title: Config knob lacks audit trail
allObjections.detail: The `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob is operator-configurable but lacks a clear audit trail. §7.6 mentions admin notification on out-of-bounds override, but not regular logging of changes.

allObjections.title: Fallback clause ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The fallback clause for re-introducing a conditional path (§11 Step 5) requires ALL `high` findings to be Resolved. However, 'Resolved' is not clearly defined in the context of Self-Renewal cycles and post-fix score reflection.

allObjections.title: Sibling charter naming inconsistency
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B-v2 switches to capability-keyed naming for sibling charters. However, the rationale does not clearly justify why this is superior to the previous agent-short-name-keyed approach, potentially introducing naming inconsistency.

allObjections.title: gtm_ready_bar_override lacks migration
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A v2 §7.6 operator-config knob section defines product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override with bounds [75,100] but names no migration path or existing-product backfill; §11 Step 5 row update references the knob without specifying how ClearanceRecord entities created pre-v2 are reconciled.

allObjections.title: fallback clause weakens hard threshold
allObjections.detail: CA-13-A v2 Near-GTM elimination section's fallback clause still permits conditional paths if Panel re-introduces them, requiring only 'Resolved' high findings; this directly conflicts with §7.6 safety-invariants (a-e) that mandate diff-only + post-deploy regression guard without defining enforcement for the fallback.

allObjections.title: EXECUTOR_REGISTRY sibling keys incomplete
allObjections.detail: CA-13-B v2 §15.1 rows 21/26 switch to capability-keyed names (crawl-write-executor, orchestra-admission-executor) but the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY typescript snippet omits required updates to BaseAgent.guard() authorityNeeded set membership and api/agent/21/execute.js wiring already referenced in §15.1.

objections.detail: CA-13-A-CT-4 conformance test only checks for conditional-clearance keywords but doesn't validate Phase B testing requirements. Agent #21's adversarial testing mandate (ENTRY 015) could be bypassed if implementation focuses solely on score thresholds without verifying interactive flow coverage.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: An operator sets gtm_ready_bar_override=95 but misses CEO's evidence prerequisite. A product scores 94.9 with zero critical issues but fails Step 5 due to HARD threshold. Under status quo, it would have cleared as Demo-ready; now it's blocked despite being market-ready, causing revenue delays.
adversarial.precedent: Google Health's 2008-2011 failure: configurable compliance thresholds without centralized enforcement led to inconsistent PHI handling across modules, causing regulatory violations. Similar to gtm_ready_bar_override without CEO-directive enforcement.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: This proposal should be deferred until after ≥1 VEU product sustains ≥95 end-to-end. Introducing configurable thresholds without evidence-backed defaults invites inconsistency, while eliminating Near-GTM bands reduces operational flexibility. The sibling naming changes create new ambiguity without solving core authority separation concerns.

CA-13-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify with tighter knob — operator override admin-only (not operator role).
CA-13-A-v2-Q1.rationale: Limiting override to admin role addresses the governance gap while preserving the evidence-based promotion principle.

CA-13-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify with reservation — fallback clause mandatory if Panel ever re-introduces a conditional path (ALL `high` findings Resolved).
CA-13-A-v2-Q2.rationale: The fallback clause provides a safety valve while maintaining the proposal's intent to eliminate risky conditional paths.

CA-13-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify with stronger language — append 'These are NEVER conflated in any operator-facing surface'.
CA-13-A-v2-Q3.rationale: Explicit anti-conflation language prevents operational confusion between Self-Audit and GTM readiness mechanisms.

CA-13-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (same as v1).
CA-13-B-v2-Q1.rationale: The ENTRY 009 alignment provides consistency, though the sibling authority pattern remains theoretically vulnerable to permission creep.

CA-13-B-v2-Q2.rationale: 'Membership' better reflects ongoing management duties beyond initial admission, aligning with §8.1 lifecycle requirements.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The knob implementation requires audit trails for CEO-directive deviations to prevent policy bypass.

objections.title: Override weakens global defaults
objections.detail: In CA-13-A v2 §7.6, `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` can raise the GTM bar per product while leaving the canonical threshold at 75. That creates a split-brain policy where the same clearance step means different things across products, environments, and operator views, increasing the chance of misconfigured launches and ambiguous audit outcomes.

objections.title: Silent clamp hides operator errors
objections.detail: The proposed `[75, 100]` clamping in CA-13-A v2 silently converts out-of-bounds values instead of rejecting them. In a governance path, silent coercion is dangerous because a mistaken `50` becomes a seemingly valid `75`, which can mask operational mistakes and make post-incident forensics harder than a hard failure would.

objections.title: Hard gate removes recovery path
objections.detail: CA-13-A v2 eliminates the 90–94 Near-GTM conditional path from §11 Step 5 entirely. That means a product that is otherwise launchable but temporarily blocked by a narrow, fixable issue cannot use a supervised conditional path, which may increase time-to-market and encourage risky workarounds outside the formal clearance flow.

objections.title: Sibling naming still underspecified
objections.detail: CA-13-B v2 switches to capability-keyed names like `crawl-write-executor` and `orchestra-admission-executor`, but the draft excerpt truncates the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY definitions and does not fully specify collision handling, lifecycle, or migration from the old keys. Without explicit compatibility rules, this risks orphaned permissions or duplicate executor entries during rollout.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If an operator sets `gtm_ready_bar_override` to 95 for a sensitive product while other teams continue to assume the canonical demo-ready bar is 75, the product can appear compliant in one layer and blocked in another. That mismatch can cause last-minute launch confusion, delayed approvals, or accidental bypasses when people rely on stale dashboards rather than the per-product registry value.
adversarial.precedent: Uber's 2018 self-driving fatality review is a real-world example of governance and safety checks being too weakly integrated with operational decision-making, with ambiguous override and monitoring practices contributing to catastrophic failure. More generally, silent coercion and policy fragmentation have repeatedly caused trouble in access-control systems such as AWS IAM misconfigurations.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring CA-13 v2 is that it changes governance semantics without enough migration and compatibility detail. The proposal introduces a per-product GTM override, removes the conditional band, and renames executor siblings, but the excerpt does not provide a complete rollout plan, compatibility matrix, or explicit remediation path for existing products and dashboards. Given that the system already treats clearance as a hard safety boundary, deferring until the implementation and observability consequences are fully specified is the safer choice.

CA-13-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted — bands UNCHANGED + knob default 75 bounds [75,100]; ≥95 re-promotes via successor CA after ≥1 VEU product proves it.
CA-13-A-v2-Q1.rationale: This is the only option that preserves the draft’s stated policy separation: canonical bands remain unchanged while ≥95 is handled as an operator-configurable per-product setting. The objection is to operational risk, not to the specific policy text as drafted.

CA-13-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted: 90–94 Near-GTM band ELIMINATED; §11 Step 5 HARD.
CA-13-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Although it reduces recovery flexibility, the draft is internally consistent that Step 5 should be hard and not admit a conditional clearance loophole. The fallback clause is only a contingency if a conditional path is reintroduced later.

CA-13-A-v2-Q3.rationale: The reconciliation paragraph usefully clarifies that the Self-Audit 95/95 threshold and the GTM Readiness bar are distinct mechanisms. That distinction is necessary to avoid conflation in operator-facing governance surfaces.

CA-13-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (same as v1).
CA-13-B-v2-Q1.rationale: The v2 text preserves the existing sibling-pattern interpretation while merely restating the lock from ENTRY 009. Since the question is about wording reconciliation, the drafted carry-forward is acceptable.

CA-13-B-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 capability-keyed naming as drafted.
CA-13-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Capability-keyed executor names are clearer than agent-short-name-keyed names because they describe function rather than lineage. That improves maintainability and reduces semantic drift in the registry.

perReviewer.overallNotes: I am not endorsing the rollout risk profile, only accepting the exact drafted text where the question asks whether the amendment should be ratified as written.

objections.title: Config knob lacks audit trail
objections.detail: The `product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override` knob is operator-configurable but lacks a clear audit trail. §7.6 mentions admin notification on out-of-bounds override, but not regular logging of changes.

objections.title: Fallback clause ambiguity
objections.detail: The fallback clause for re-introducing a conditional path (§11 Step 5) requires ALL `high` findings to be Resolved. However, 'Resolved' is not clearly defined in the context of Self-Renewal cycles and post-fix score reflection.

objections.title: Sibling charter naming inconsistency
objections.detail: CA-13-B-v2 switches to capability-keyed naming for sibling charters. However, the rationale does not clearly justify why this is superior to the previous agent-short-name-keyed approach, potentially introducing naming inconsistency.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the `gtm_ready_bar_override` knob is misused or set too high without proper oversight, it could lead to products being cleared for GTM without meeting the intended quality thresholds, potentially harming customer experience and trust.
adversarial.precedent: The configurable GTM readiness bar with operator override has a similar design pattern to Kubernetes' admission controllers, where certain checks can be bypassed or configured. However, Kubernetes also emphasizes audit logging for such configurations.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal could be deferred because it introduces a new configuration knob without a comprehensive audit and change tracking mechanism, which is critical for governance and traceability in production environments.

CA-13-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify with tighter knob — operator override admin-only (not operator role).
CA-13-A-v2-Q1.rationale: Restricting the override to admin role adds a layer of governance and reduces the risk of misuse.

CA-13-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted: 90–94 Near-GTM band ELIMINATED; §11 Step 5 HARD.
CA-13-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Eliminating the conditional clearance path aligns with the intent of maintaining high quality thresholds for GTM readiness.

CA-13-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify with stronger language — append 'These are NEVER conflated in any operator-facing surface'.
CA-13-A-v2-Q3.rationale: Adding stronger language clarifies the distinction between Self-Audit 95/95 and GTM Readiness bar, reducing potential confusion.

CA-13-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (same as v1).
CA-13-B-v2-Q1.rationale: The v2 retains the v1 wording for §15-intro and §15.1 rows 21/26, which have been previously reviewed and deemed acceptable.

CA-13-B-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 capability-keyed naming as drafted.
CA-13-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Capability-keyed naming provides clarity on the function of the sibling charters, which is beneficial for understanding and maintaining the system.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal addresses several concerns raised in the previous Panel review, but careful implementation and monitoring of the new configuration knob are crucial.

objections.title: gtm_ready_bar_override lacks migration
objections.detail: CA-13-A v2 §7.6 operator-config knob section defines product_registry.gtm_ready_bar_override with bounds [75,100] but names no migration path or existing-product backfill; §11 Step 5 row update references the knob without specifying how ClearanceRecord entities created pre-v2 are reconciled.

objections.title: fallback clause weakens hard threshold
objections.detail: CA-13-A v2 Near-GTM elimination section's fallback clause still permits conditional paths if Panel re-introduces them, requiring only 'Resolved' high findings; this directly conflicts with §7.6 safety-invariants (a-e) that mandate diff-only + post-deploy regression guard without defining enforcement for the fallback.

objections.title: EXECUTOR_REGISTRY sibling keys incomplete
objections.detail: CA-13-B v2 §15.1 rows 21/26 switch to capability-keyed names (crawl-write-executor, orchestra-admission-executor) but the EXECUTOR_REGISTRY typescript snippet omits required updates to BaseAgent.guard() authorityNeeded set membership and api/agent/21/execute.js wiring already referenced in §15.1.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: An operator sets gtm_ready_bar_override=95 on a product that previously cleared at the canonical 75 Demo-ready band; the product now fails §11 Step 5 indefinitely despite passing all other gates, blocking demos that status-quo ENTRY 006 bands would have allowed.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The v2 draft layers operator-configurable overrides and fallback clauses onto an already complex multi-gate clearance system (§11, §19, §7.6) without demonstrated production evidence or migration tooling; this risks governance fragmentation and configuration drift that could erode the canonical SSOT guarantees more than retaining the simpler ENTRY 006 bands.

CA-13-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v2-Q1.rationale: All options either ratify an unproven knob or demand immediate canonical change; none addresses the missing migration path for existing ClearanceRecord entities.

CA-13-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Retaining any fallback clause re-introduces conditional paths that contradict the hard-threshold intent and §7.6 invariants.

CA-13-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-A-v2-Q3.rationale: §19.0 remains redundant with the §19 governance table and adds no enforceable distinction between the two 95 bars.

CA-13-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-13-B-v2-Q1.rationale: The sibling-pattern wording still lacks concrete BaseAgent.guard() and EXECUTOR_REGISTRY enforcement details.

CA-13-B-v2-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
